name: Altar
text: An ornamental place of ritual worship, such as a raised dais.

name: Animal Pen
text: An enclosure for one or more animals, often a familiar, to dwell.

name: Antechamber
text: A separate enclosure or compartment. Spells may be cast here in a more secure environment.

name: Astronomical Device
text: A sophisticated tool for measuring the movements of the heavens, often placed near a window or skylight. The most common such item is an astrolabe; and example of a more advanced device is the armillary sphere.

name: Balance
text: An exact weighing device, such as a pair of scales.

name: Balcony
text: An outdoors balcony, where the magus may cast spells into the open air.

name: Cage
text: A large cage, usually built of sturdy metal bars, for imprisoning or immobilizing a subject.

name: Cauldron
text: A heavy copper or brass cauldron, for the heating and mixing of large quantities of ingredients.

name: Desk
text: A comfortable and stout table, designed for reading and scribing.

name: Fireplace
text: A stone enclosure, where fuel is burnt for heating, but where substances may also be heated or immolated.

name: Forge
text: A furnace — a more tightly enclosed and robust fireplace often operated by bellows, which yields heat sufficient for the smelting of metals — accompanied by an anvil and smithy.

name: Grave
text: The burial place of one or more corpses. This may be either a simple earthen grave or something more elaborate, such as a stone sarcophagus.

name: Lofty Ceiling
text: A light, airy space overhead, for which a tall chamber, perhaps with a vaulted ceiling, is required.

name: Loom
text: A large wooden apparatus for the weaving of threads into a fabric.

name: Map
text: An elaborate and detailed plan or model, accurately illustrating surrounding lands or buildings, perhaps.

name: Mechanism
text: Any kind of large mechanical device, consisting of many moving parts such as cogs and wheels, used for the basic automation of one or more tasks.

name: Mirror
text: A grand and ornamental silvered mirror, or other reflective surface.

name: Monolith
text: A huge slab of primal rock, possibly carved with mystical symbols.

name: Orb
text: A smooth sphere of precious stone, possibly opaque or semi-opaque, used in conjunction with divinatory effects.

name: Pallet
text: A bed upon which a patient may be treated or examined, perhaps equipped with some surgeon's tools.

name: Pit
text: A deep hole dug in the floor. Things placed inside it cannot easily get out.

name: Pool
text: A still body of water, or a well. It may be used when scrying.

name: Portal
text: A gateway, through which things may be summoned or sent away.

name: Rack
text: A rather unpleasant large mechanical construct, used for torturing persons placed inside it.

name: Running Water
text: Any kind of water which runs through or around the lab, such as a stream or fountain.

name: Summoning Circle
text: An elaborate pentagram marked on the floor, into which things are summoned.

name: Statue
text: A carved semblance of some person, creature, or thing, usually made of stone, metal, or porcelain.

name: Still
text: A network of glass or metal tubing connecting delicate containers, such as retorts, designed for the distillation and refinement of compounds.

name: Tablet
text: A large framed slab of wax, for temporary scribing with a stylus.

name: Tank
text: A bulky container for storing fluids.

name: Throne
text: An opulent and raised seat for a ruler (or at least, the self-important) to sit in.

name: Tree
text: A live tree or a large plant, such as a vine.

name: Void
text: A shaft, hole, or opening.

name: Wall
text: A large blank wall, onto which images may be summoned.

name: Wheel
text: A wheel powered by water, wind, horse, slaves, or magic.

name: Window
text: A portal to the outside world, which lets in the sun, moon, and stars.
